title: American Samoa, led by Taulia Tagovailoa, stuns U.S. at Flag Football World Championships
content:
American Samoa, led by Taulia Tagovailoa, delivered a stunner during group play at the IFAF Flag Football World Championships in Düsseldorf, Germany, handing the U.S. its first loss at the event since 2012.

Tagovailoa, the 26-year-old former Maryland quarterback and younger brother of NFL quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, threw five touchdowns and completed 29 of 36 passes for 213 yards in the 38-32 win Friday. The loss ended a 14-year undefeated streak for the men’s U.S. flag football team at the world championships. The Americans’ previous loss was to Austria in the 2012 final.

The U.S scored the game’s opening touchdown less than two minutes into the first half, but American Samoa answered with two consecutive touchdowns to take a one-score lead. Later in the half, the U.S. took a 13-12 lead after a touchdown and successful two-point conversion. However, American Samoa returned the favor — and then some. It closed the half with a touchdown and two-point conversion, then scored an early second-half touchdown to take a 26-13 lead, its largest of the game after a successful two-point try with 15 minutes remaining.

The U.S. responded with a touchdown on its ensuing possession, but Tagovailoa unleashed two more deep balls that resulted in TDs, sealing the win despite one final U.S. touchdown.

The U.S. bounced back later Friday with a dominating 40-7 win over Australia to advance to the quarterfinals in its final group-play game. The U.S. women, who’ve won the previous three world titles, are 3-0 in group play and will face Germany on Saturday in the quarterfinals.

Flag football will make its Olympic debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. The U.S. has already secured two spots as Olympic hosts, so if the U.S. places in the top two in either the men’s or women’s, the bronze-medal-winning team will automatically receive a bid.
